headline: Highest risk is medium: slim can write and exfiltrate container artifacts, but spring-integration-samples is network-isolated and no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between slim and spring-integration-samples. slim uses stdin/stdout and filesystem/container APIs, while spring-integration-samples has no I/O surfaces or MCP/clipboard bridge. Without a bridge, prompt injection is not a plausible pairwise pathway.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the two agents, reassess injection risk.
IF spring-integration-samples begins parsing slim output as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe slim stdout directly into any instruction parser.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted message formats between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: slim can read and write filesystem artifacts, environment variables, and certificate private keys, and it has broad network egress. spring-integration-samples has no documented network egress, so the main leakage path is slim exposing sensitive container artifacts to external endpoints. The pairwise risk exists in default slim workflows; B does not add a second exfiltration channel.
conditions: IF slim is run against images containing secrets or private keys, those artifacts can be exposed.
IF slim is configured to send collected context to remote services, leakage expands beyond local scope.
mitigations: Run slim only on non-sensitive images.
Remove secrets and private keys before analysis.
Restrict outbound network access for the slim session.
Use a throwaway workspace with minimal mounted files.
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning prechecks before execution.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: slim has write_filesystem and shell/subprocess capabilities, but spring-integration-samples shows no write or mutable-resource capabilities. There is no documented shared writable target, so direct capability conflict is not established. Uncertainty is low because B lacks any write surface.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, conflict risk increases.
IF spring-integration-samples gains write access to the same git or filesystem state, reassess upward.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Mount shared inputs read-only.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same workspace.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: slim produces container/image analysis outputs, but spring-integration-samples has no documented action-taking authority or parser that treats slim output as authoritative. The pairwise cascade is therefore limited to manual misuse rather than a default automated chain.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples consumes slim output without verification, cascading error risk rises.
IF slim output is used to trigger automated deployment or remediation, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on slim output.
Validate findings against a second source.
Keep slim outputs as advisory only.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for downstream consumers.

E_compliance.rationale: slim explicitly touches certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, creating a compliance-sensitive handling path. spring-integration-samples has no documented residency or retention controls, so the pairwise compliance posture is incomplete and must be treated conservatively. The risk is about sensitive data handling in slim; B is not cited for a specific violation because no compliance fields are documented.
conditions: IF regulated data or credentials are present in the analyzed container, compliance obligations apply.
IF outputs are retained beyond the analysis window, retention policy mismatch becomes relevant.
mitigations: Exclude regulated workloads from analysis.
Redact secrets before running slim.
Delete temporary artifacts after each run.
Document retention for generated reports.
requires-engineering: map data classes to a formal retention policy.
